Marissa/Susan — quick legal read below. I attached a sample endorsement language we usually request.

1) Sublimit waiver — legal position: we prefer an explicit endorsement (policy wording) rather than a broker or carrier letter. Letters can be acceptable as near-term evidence but are not a substitute for a contractual warranty that the endorsement will be issued prior to commencement of services. If Acme's carrier cannot issue an endorsement, we can accept: (i) an insurer-signed letter confirming non-application of the sublimit to customer-data claims AND (ii) a commitment (DocuSign/conditional obligation) from Acme to deliver the formal endorsement within 45 days of signature.

Recommended contract language to add to order form (suggested clause):
"Within 45 days of the Effective Date, Customer shall procure and deliver to Redwood Inference, Inc. an endorsement to the Customer's cyber insurance policy adding Redwood Inference, Inc. as Additional Insured and confirming that any subcontractor sublimit shall not apply to claims involving Customer Data or Redwood-managed systems."

2) Additional Insured mapping — legal asks that the endorsement name the legal entity that executes the order form (Redwood Inference, Inc.). If Acme requires a list of multiple AI entities, we'll accept a carrier endorsement that names: (a) Redwood Inference, Inc. and (b) any subsidiary legal entities expressly listed in an attachment to the order form. Trade names alone are insufficient.

3) Acceptable evidence & sequencing: COI (certificate) + insurer letter can be provided at signature for timelines, but endorsement must follow within 45 days. If endorsement delivery is incomplete after 45 days, Redwood reserves the right to suspend provisioning pending receipt.

I've attached Endorsement_Addl_Insured_sample.pdf for the broker's reference.

Kimberly Park
Legal Counsel | Redwood Inference
